key_insight: Light can reversibly switch halide ions in 2D mixed-halide perovskites through strong light-lattice coupling, enabling a defect-free photoresponse that resets when illumination is removed.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a route to reversible optoelectronic devices and photo-tunable perovskite components without relying on defect-driven degradation.
method: NEB calculations mapped the halide-exchange energy pathway.
Photo-force calculations quantified non-equilibrium work from illumination.
GW-based electronic structure and lattice-dynamics analysis linked bandgap renormalization to soft, IR-active phonon modes.
evidence_signal: The study reproduces experimental absorption spectra at equilibrium and predicts a clear light-induced redshift consistent with photo-induced bandgap renormalization.
watch_item: The mechanism depends on specific light-lattice coupling in 2D mixed-halide perovskites, so device stability and switching strength may vary with composition, thickness, and illumination conditions.
paper_title: Reversible photo-switching optical functionality in two-dimensional mixed-halide hybrid perovskites
